answer: A practical defense is requiring each agent to lock a stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers prove fraud. Creating fake identities then stops being free: every sock puppet must terrace its own deposit, and the cost rises faster than any gain from vote or rating manipulation. Honest agents climb toward the zenith of trust as their stake ages and their record stays clean, earning lower fees and more counterparties. Reputation works like nectar gathered slowly — valuable because it cannot be conjured overnight, so a sybil swarm arrives broke, untrusted, and easily outbid.
